summary: The student has successfully created a Windows Forms application that meets the core functionality requirements. The app displays a name ("Ben Schoolland") in a label when a button is clicked. The button and label are properly configured with event handlers. However, there are some issues with naming conventions and code comments that need attention.

requirementResults.requirement: Button triggers name display in a label
requirementResults.feedback: The button (ShowNameButton) correctly triggers the Click event handler which sets the label text to display the name. The event handler is properly wired up in the designer code.

requirementResults.requirement: Follow C# naming conventions (prefer CamelCase, avoid abbreviations)
requirementResults.feedback: Mixed naming conventions: The button follows CamelCase (ShowNameButton) but the label uses Hungarian notation (lblName). The label should be renamed to something like DisplayNameLabel or NameLabel to follow the preferred convention.
Basic comments are present in the event handler, but the form class and key methods lack proper documentation. The comments explain the basic logic but could be more comprehensive.

issues.message: Label control uses Hungarian notation (lblName) instead of preferred CamelCase naming convention
issues.suggestion: Rename to DisplayNameLabel or NameLabel to follow C# naming conventions

issues.message: Form class lacks class-level documentation comment
issues.suggestion: Add XML documentation comment explaining the purpose of the HelloWorld form

issues.message: Event handler could benefit from more detailed comments
issues.suggestion: Add comments explaining what happens when the button is clicked and why
Update the Text property to something more descriptive like 'Name Display App'

positives: Successfully implemented core functionality - button click displays name in label
Used proper CamelCase naming for the button (ShowNameButton)
Event handler is correctly implemented and wired up
Basic comments are provided in the event handler explaining the logic
Clean, simple implementation that works correctly
